How to Submit an Event or Request a New Calendar

If you are part of NYU Grossman School of Medicine and would like to submit an event, choose a specific calendar and click the “Submit an Event” button, and then log in with your Kerberos ID and password to complete the event submission form. Your request will be reviewed by the calendar’s manager.

To request a new calendar, please fill out a public website content request form. For the Request Type field, select med.nyu.edu and then provide the details about your new calendar request. events.name: Communication Design Graduate Reception 2026
events.description: Join us for a toast to honor the class of 2026 from our AAS, BFA, and MPS Communication Design programs. This event offers a great chance to connect with faculty and celebrate with peers, family, and friends. Our students have traveled from around the globe and across the country, dedicating four years to exploring design, university life, and the city’s culture. As they move forward into a world filled with new opportunities and challenges, they remain optimistic about the impact of design globally. We will also mark the release of Framework 105, the catalog showcasing the exceptional work produced by the class of 2026.

events.name: BFA Fashion Runway Livestream 2026
events.description: We invite you to join us for the livestream of "ENSEMBLE," the Parsons BFA Fashion 2026 Runway Show, featuring a curated lineup of student thesis work. The show will be broadcast below at 3:00PM on Sunday, May 17. Please also visit our Instagram account, @parsons_fashion, for a behind-the-scenes look leading up to the livestream. The BFA Fashion Design program would like to acknowledge our partners for this event. We are grateful for the support of Theory for our 2026 End of Year programming, and We Speak Model Management, for models and casting services.

events.name: Truth Be Told - 18th Annual Documentary Film Festival
events.description: An Evening of Original Documentary Shorts The Graduate Certificate in Documentary Media Studies is proud to present Truth be Told, its eighteenth annual festival of original short films made by students in the class of 2026.Each work is the result of a year of intensive study in documentary cinema production, history, theory, and aesthetics. Hosted by Amir Husak, Director of the Documentary Media Studies Graduate Certificate Program at The New School. Co-produced with Documentary Program Associates Arushi Kalia (Media Studies '26) and Guili Mikovicious (Media Management '26). The screenings will be followed by a faculty-led Q & A with the filmmakers and a light reception. Admission is free and open to the public. Registration is required. **Full program to be announced shortly** For information about the Doc Studies program, please visit the Doc Studies website.

events.name: Parsons Paris Commencement 2026
events.description: The 2026 Parsons Paris Commencement celebration will take place on Friday, May 22, 2026 at the historic Le Grand Rex theatre located at 1 Bd Poissonnière, 75002 Paris.The ceremony will take place in the Grande Salle auditorium at 11:00 am, immediately followed by a champagne toast with salty and savory appetizers on the orchestra, mezzanine and balcony levels until 2:00 pm.Access to the venue is via metro lines 8 and 9, stop Bonne Nouvelle, or via bus lines 20, 32 and 39, stop Poissonière-Bonne Nouvelle. We look forward to seeing our graduates and their guests to celebrate the accomplishments of the Class of 2026 at this important milestone!

events.name: Parsons Scholars Graduation and Capstone 2026
events.description: For the last two and a half years, our Scholars have had the joy and pleasure of working hard to complete the Parsons Scholars Program. These incredible young individuals explored their interest in art and design and began their transition toward their futures and careers. Now, we would like to gather our community to celebrate their graduation commencement on May 22nd at The New School!

events.name: The Remembering
events.description: The Remembering is a capsule collection and immersive experience by Naika Colas exploring Haitian agricultural memory, diasporic identity, and the stories carried across generations through the art of garment-making.Rooted in the life and legacy of the designer’s grandmother, the collection translates land and lineage into hand-sewn garments which are created in collaboration with the women of Sewing for Refuge, a nonprofit initiative supporting refugee and asylum-seeking garment workers in New York City.This multidisciplinary event brings together a fashion presentation, curated food experience, and panel discussion alongside a vibrant cultural program featuring Haitian vendors, performers, and artists. Guests will experience contributions from Papa Rozier, as well as live Haitian dancers, singers, and visual artists whose work reflects the richness and continuity of Haitian culture.The evening’s conversation will be moderated by philanthropist, strategist, and freelance writer Ruth Jean-Marie, guiding a dialogue at the intersection of fashion, culture, and community.The Remembering invites attendees to engage with fashion as both material and memory, offering a space where design, storytelling, and community converge.

events.name: Silver Tsunami or Silver Rush? Extracting Value from Elders
events.description: Join us for the first installment of the Reimagining the Economics of Aging Seminar Series, a monthly virtual forum hosted by the Wealth Equity Lab at The New School. Building on our May 1 conference, this series brings together scholars and practitioners to deepen conversations on aging, retirement, and late-life economic security, with a focus on works in progress and active discussion.In this session, Andrew Milne examines how the U.S. elder care financing system not only fails older adults but actively produces inequality. Drawing on real-world legal cases, he reveals how low-income elders—whether homeowners or renters—are funneled into systems that extract value from their care needs, often culminating in institutionalization. The talk explores the privatization of Medicare and the legal dynamics shaping access to housing and care, arguing that these are not isolated failures but systemic outcomes. Milne ultimately calls for structural change while considering the role of incremental reforms in building collective power. Read the full paper here: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5165338About the speaker: Andrew Milne is the Bruce R. Jacob Visiting Assistant Professor of Law (2025–2027), whose research draws on over a decade of practice in poverty law and disability rights. His work focuses on the intersection of law, aging, and political economy, informed by extensive experience representing older adults and vulnerable populations across multiple legal settings.This event is part of the Reimagining the Economics of Aging Seminar Series

events.name: The Mentor's Action Plan Convening 2026
events.description: Credible Community Circles: A Trust-Building approach to restoring community leadership and Restorative Justice work—led by Credible messengers. The 2026 Map Convening will serve as the culmination of two years dedicated to the Mentor's Action Plan (MAP)—trainings for Credible Messengers to implement Community Circles that are deemed Credible by their neighbors. These Credible Community Circles are intergenerational practices that are facilitated by 19 MAP Fellows, each representing a grassroots organization in a community they’re connected to. To date, ITM has funded and supported 19 organizations performing services throughout NYC and beyond, facilitating circles and strengthening community ties. On June 4, 2026, at the start of Gun Violence Awareness month, we invite you to engage in discussions about credible messengers, restorative practices, and the vital intersection of trust-building efforts that are essential for enhancing community and Community-Based Restorative Justice work.

events.description:
<p>We are pleased to invite you to a special symposium on <strong>June 8</strong> celebrating the distinguished career and scientific legacy of Dr. Robert &quot;Rocky&quot; Kass, former Chair of the Department of Pharmacology and Vice Dean for Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. This full-day event will feature presentations from former trainees and colleagues, highlighting seminal contributions and ongoing advances inspired by his&nbsp;work in biomedical research. The program will span foundational discoveries, emerging directions, and personal reflections, culminating in remarks from the honoree.</p>
<p>We hope you will join us for this unique opportunity to celebrate a remarkable career and the enduring impact of a vibrant scientific community. Registration is <strong>required</strong> and will be open until <strong>June 1.</strong></p>

This year&rsquo;s program brings together practicing ophthalmologists, optometrists, trainees, and ophthalmic team members for an immersive learning experience.</p>
